title: Sharp Sensitivity Bounds for the Mortality-Income Concentration Index under Treatment-Odds Departures
banked_reason: The promised Stat contribution—same-record minimax risk and honest-interval frontiers with total estimators—is expressly deferred and has been replaced by a population-access partial-identification sensitivity certificate; this cannot support the declared Stat anchor or its rate-based novelty claim.
gap_reasons: The promised Stat contribution—same-record minimax risk and honest-interval frontiers with total estimators—is expressly deferred and has been replaced by a population-access partial-identification sensitivity certificate; this cannot support the declared Stat anchor or its rate-based novelty claim.

The certificate reproduction uses only measurability plus the two uniform covariate Hölder bounds (to obtain the cell-mass bound); treated joint continuity is never consumed, so the theorem is stated on a materially narrower class than its proof establishes.
proof_attempt_summary: The original all-alpha same-record minimax and honest-interval program failed to establish field novelty and was replaced by a joint odds-sensitivity endpoint angle. D0 discharged the sensitivity graph, but D0.5 rejected the substitution and graded the achieved artifact incremental (paper-score ceiling 4.5); restoring the original program requires new estimator, rate, coverage, and lower-bound theorems. No Lean formalization ran; the unused treated-joint-continuity assumption is preserved and disclosed in the frozen artifact.
tldr: The relative mortality-income concentration index has sharp bounds over all joint intervention laws compatible with the observed records and a finite public treatment-odds departure. One normalized joint law generates the mortality mean, intervention income ranks and marked-rank numerator. The observed rare envelopes imply a positive mortality bound and atomless income before the ratio is evaluated. The endpoint theorem distinguishes validity from attainment and gives compatible full-data witnesses, an exact global residual characterization and a critical sign-reversal consequence. The sole open deliverable is certified finite population evaluation of these coupled endpoints. The target and normalization match the joint-law branch of the final Biometrics concentration-index paper at odds departure one. No estimation frontier, confidence-envelope or limit-law contribution is claimed.
gap: The final concentration-index paper identifies the dependent joint-law target and calls for sensitivity analysis in Section 5. Its scalar-tilt and residual-correlation mean references do not give the same joint odds-compatible endpoint problem. Sharp fixed-score mean bounds cannot simply be combined when the optimized joint law also generates the marginal ranks.
fill: The full-law endpoint characterization, compatible endpoint completions, exact global self-consistency and critical odds infima define one sensitivity result. Finite population evaluation with feasible inner laws and global outer certificates is its open computational obligation.
